# 1 Enoch Chapter 82 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn-astr (Aramaic) | **Section:** Astronomical Book (Book of Luminaries)

---

**1** "Now, my son Methuselah — I am recounting all these things to you and writing them down for you. I have revealed everything and given you books about all of it. Preserve these books from your father's hand, and make sure you pass them on to future generations."

**2** "I have given wisdom to you and to your children, and to the children they will have in turn — so that it will be passed down through the generations. This is a wisdom that surpasses ordinary understanding.

**3** Those who truly grasp it will not sleep — they will listen carefully to learn it, and it will satisfy them more than the finest food."

**4** Blessed are all the righteous — blessed are all who walk the path of righteousness without sinning as the sinners do. They count their days rightly: the sun traveling through heaven, entering and exiting through its gates across thirty days, along with the leaders of the star-ranks and the four intercalary days that divide the four seasons of the year.

**5** Because of those four days, people make errors — they fail to count them in the yearly total, and so they miscalculate.

**6** But those four days are genuinely part of the year and are recorded there forever — one in the first gate, one in the third, one in the fourth, and one in the sixth. The year is thus completed in three hundred and sixty-four days.

**7** The reckoning is accurate and the record is exact. Uriel revealed all of this to me — the luminaries, months, festivals, years, and days — Uriel to whom the Lord of all creation has entrusted the heavenly host.

**8** He has authority over night and day in heaven, to direct light to people — the sun, the moon, and the stars, and all the powers of heaven traveling in their circular chariots.

**9** These are the ranks of the stars, stationed in their appointed places, following their seasons, festivals, and months.

**10** These are the names of their leaders — those who ensure they arrive on time, in their proper order, in their seasons, months, periods of rule, and assigned positions.

**11** First come the four leaders who divide the four seasons of the year. Then come the twelve leaders of the monthly ranks. For the three hundred and sixty regular days there are captains over thousands who manage each day. And for the four intercalary days there are leaders who mark the four seasonal divisions.

**12** These captains over thousands are positioned between the primary leaders, each stationed behind his post; but the primary leaders make the actual divisions.

**13** The names of the leaders who divide the four seasons are: Milki'el, Hel'emmelek, Mele'jal, and Narel.

**14** The names of those who serve under them are Adnar'el, Ijasusa'el, and Elome'el — three who follow the rank-leaders — plus one more who follows those three in turn.

**15** At the beginning of the year, Milki'el rises first and takes command — he is also called Tam'aini, the Sun. His period of rule lasts ninety-one days.

**16** During his days, these are the signs visible on earth: heat and perspiration, calm weather; all the trees bear fruit, leaves grow on every tree; there is the wheat harvest, the flowering of roses, all the flowers of the field; but the winter trees become bare.

**17** His subordinate leaders are Kesfael, Kemal, and Kaup; and the one who leads those three is Asfa'el. His period of rule is ninety-one days.

**18** Then the second quarter begins: Hel'emmelek takes command — he is called the Shining Sun — and his period of light lasts ninety-one days.

**19** During his days, these are the signs on earth: blazing heat and drought; the trees fully ripen their fruit and produce an abundant harvest; the flocks mate and become pregnant; all the earth's produce is gathered in, everything in the fields, and the pressing of the wine — all of this happens during his dominion.

**20** His subordinate leaders are Gida'ljal, Ke'el, and He'el; the captain over them is Asfa'el; and his period of rule is ninety-one days.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic equivalence rendering. Chapter 82 closes the Astronomical Book with Enoch's transmission to Methuselah and the naming of the four angelic seasonal rulers: Milki'el (spring, 91 days), Hel'emmelek (summer, 91 days), Mele'jal (autumn, 91 days), Narel (winter, 91 days). Each season has its own angelic hierarchy — a remarkable synthesis of astronomy, angelology, and agriculture. The seasonal signs (wheat harvest in spring, winepress in summer) reflect Palestinian agricultural reality.*
